correctness.rationale: The relation T_(j+1)=bT_j+1 sends each noninitial plateau back to the preceding plateau under the integer parent map; the plateau lengths b^j give the normalized backward digit sum at T_j. The normalization correction and the missing iid past are separately between 0 and b^(-j), so their difference has absolute value at most b^(-j). Birkhoff for a countable dense family of continuous tests gives simultaneous weak convergence to the weighted Bernoulli digit law. Every finite digit word occurs arbitrarily far out, giving exactly the compact coding set as the endpoint cluster set. Long constant runs give extremes 0 and 1, and jumps bounded by 1/(N+1) force every intermediate all-time cluster value. Summing squared weights gives the stated variance; the open-set condition includes the b=2 endpoint-touching case, giving H(p)/log b by the Bernoulli self-similar measure dimension theorem. Fair binary digits give Lebesgue measure; every other stated case has dimension less than one. The finite rational checker and its recorded output were inspected, not rerun or used for the infinite conclusions.
residual_risks: The cited Hutchinson passage verifies support dimension and the canonical weights, not the arbitrary-bias formula by itself; the latter uses the standard entropy formula under the open-set condition. The conclusions are for fixed b,p and the specified coordinate observable only.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The pushforward law itself and its dimension are classical. The additional identification at one sampling sequence and the contrasting cluster set at the other are not just renaming a prior statement about the tent-map observable or the known self-similar measure.

originality.rationale: Credit the proportional-delay plateaus, qualitative failure of time-average agreement, and classical self-similar measures to prior work. The distinct claim supported by the inspected evidence is the almost-sure joint description for the same delayed Bernoulli observable: full physical-time cluster interval versus the endpoint coding set, together with the endpoint empirical distribution. Neither the closest tent-map statements nor the classical coding results state or establish this comparison for the digit observable.

value.rationale: This is a tractable exact test case for how the sampling clock changes an empirical observable. For b≥3 the endpoint cluster set actually has gaps that all-time sampling fills, and the endpoint frequency of visits is specified rather than merely shown not to converge to the undelayed mean. This supplies a useful model distinction, not a novelty claim for Bernoulli measures or Birkhoff's theorem.
residual_risks: No implication is claimed for arbitrary observables, other delays, or the empirical measure of the underlying state sequence.
